2.t: These are the verses of the Scripture that makes things clear:

3.t: [Prophet], are you going to worry yourself to death because they will not believe?

4.t: If We had wished, We could have sent them down a sign from heaven, at which their necks would stay bowed in utter humility.

5.t: Whenever they are brought a new revelation from the Lord of Mercy, they turn away:

6.t: they deny it, but the truth of what they scorned will soon hit them.

7.t: Do they not see the earth, and what noble kinds of thing We grow in it?

8.t: There truly is a sign in this, though most of them do not believe:

9.t: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.

10.t: Your Lord called to Moses: ‘Go to those wrongdoers,

11.t: the people of Pharaoh. Will they not take heed?’

12.t: Moses said, ‘My Lord, I fear they will call me a liar,

13.t: and I will feel stressed and tongue-tied, so send Aaron too;

14.t: besides, they have a chargeagainst me, and I fear they may kill me.’

15.t: God said, ‘No [they will not]. Go, both of you, with Our signs––We shall be with you, listen-ing.

16.t: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh and say, “We bring a message from the Lord of the Worlds:

17.t: let the Children of Israel leave with us.” ’

18.t: Pharaoh said, ‘Did we not bring you up as a child among us? Did you not stay with us for many years?

19.t: And then you committed that crime of yours: you were so ungrateful.’

20.t: Moses replied, ‘I was misguided when I did it

21.t: and I fled from you in fear; later my Lord gave me wisdom and made me one of His messengers.

22.t: And is this- that you have enslaved the Children of Israel- the favour with which you reproach me?’

23.t: Pharaoh asked, ‘What is this “Lord of the Worlds”?’

24.t: Moses replied, ‘He is the Lord of the heavens and earth and everything between them. If you would only have faith!’

25.t: Pharaoh said to those present, ‘Do you hear what he says?’

26.t: Moses said, ‘He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.’

27.t: Pharaoh said, ‘This messenger who has been sent to you is truly possessed.’

28.t: Moses continued, ‘Lord of the East and West and everything between them. If you would only use your reason!’

29.t: But Pharaoh said [to him], ‘If you take any god other than me, I will throw you into prison,’

30.t: and Moses asked, ‘Even if I show you something convincing?’

31.t: ‘Show it then,’ said Pharaoh, ‘if you are telling the truth.’

32.t: So Moses threw down his staff and- lo and behold!- it became a snake for everyone to see.

33.t: Then he drew out his hand and- lo and behold!- it was white for the onlookers to see.

34.t: Pharaoh said to the counsellors around him, ‘This man is a learned sorcerer!

35.t: He means to use his sorcery to drive you out of your land! What do you suggest?’

36.t: They answered, ‘Delay him and his brother for a while, and send messengers to all the cities

37.t: to bring every accomplished sorcerer to you.’

38.t: The sorcerers were [to be] assembled at the appointed time on a certain day

39.t: and the people were asked, "Are you all coming?

40.t: We may follow the sorcerers if they win!"

41.t: When the sorcerers came, they said to Pharaoh, ‘Shall we be rewarded if we win?’

42.t: and he said, ‘Yes, and you will join my inner court.’

43.t: Moses said to them, ‘Throw down whatever you will.’

44.t: They threw their ropes and staffs, saying, ‘By Pharaoh’s might, we shall be victorious.’

45.t: But Moses threw his staff and- lo and behold!- it swallowed up their trickery

46.t: and the sorcerers fell down on their knees,

47.t: exclaiming, ‘We believe in the Lord of the Worlds,

48.t: the Lord of Moses and Aaron.’

49.t: Pharaoh said, ‘How dare you believe in him before I have given you permission? He must be the master who taught you sorcery! Soon you will see: I will cut off your alternate hands and feet and then crucify the lot of you!’

50.t: ‘That will do us no harm,’ they said, ‘for we are sure to return to our Lord.

51.t: We hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, as we were the first to believe.’

52.t: Then We revealed Our will to Moses, ‘Leave with My servants by night, for you will be pursued!’

53.t: Pharaoh sent messengers into the cities, proclaiming,

56.t: and we are a large army, on the alert.’

57.t: So it was that We made them leave their gardens and their springs,

58.t: their treasures and their noble dwellings-

59.t: We gave [such] things [later]to the Children of Israel.

60.t: Pharaoh and his people pursued them at sunrise,

61.t: and as soon as the two sides came within sight of one another, Moses’ followers said, ‘We shall definitely be caught.’

62.t: Moses said, ‘No, my Lord is with me: He will guide me,’

63.t: and We revealed to Moses: ‘Strike the sea with your staff.’ It parted- each side like a mighty mountain-

64.t: and We brought the others to that place:

65.t: We saved Moses and all his companions,

67.t: There truly is a sign in this, though most of them do not believe:

68.t: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.

69.t: Tell them the story of Abraham,

70.t: when he asked his father and his people, ‘What do you worship?’

71.t: They said, ‘We worship idols, and are constantly in attendance on them.’

72.t: He asked, ‘Do they hear you when you call?

73.t: Do they help or harm you?’

74.t: They replied, ‘No, but this is what we saw our fathers doing.’

75.t: Abraham said, ‘Those idols you have worshipped,

77.t: are my enemies; not so the Lord of the Worlds,

78.t: who created me. It is He who guides me;

79.t: He who gives me food and drink;

80.t: He who cures me when I am ill;

81.t: He who will make me die and then give me life again;

82.t: and He who will, I hope, forgive my faults on the Day of Judgement.

83.t: My Lord, grant me wisdom; join me with the righteous;

84.t: give me a good name among later generations;

85.t: make me one of those given the Garden of Bliss-

86.t: forgive my father, for he is one of those who have gone astray-

87.t: and do not disgrace me on the Day when all people are resurrected:

88.t: the Day when neither wealth nor children can help,

89.t: when the only one who will be saved is the one who comes before God with a heart devoted to Him.’

90.t: When the Garden is brought near to the righteous

91.t: and the Fire is placed in full view of the misguided,

92.t: it will be said to them, ‘Where are those you worshipped

93.t: beside God? Can they help you now, or even help themselves?’

94.t: and then they will all be hurled into Hell, together with those that misled them,

96.t: There they will say to their gods, as they bicker among themselves,

98.t: when we made you equal with the Lord of the Worlds.

99.t: It was the evildoers who led us astray,

100.t: and now we have no intercessor

102.t: If only we could live our lives again, we would be true believers!’

103.t: There truly is a sign in this, though most of them do not believe:

104.t: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.

105.t: The people of Noah, too, called the messengers liars.

106.t: Their brother Noah said to them, ‘Will you not be mindful of God?

107.t: I am a faithful messenger sent to you:

108.t: be mindful of God and obey me.

109.t: I ask no reward of you, for my only reward is with the Lord of the Worlds:

110.t: be mindful of God and obey me.’

111.t: They answered, ‘Why should we believe you when the worst sort of people follow you?’

112.t: He said, ‘What knowledge do I have of what they used to do?

113.t: It is for my Lord alone to bring them to account- if only you could see-

114.t: I will not drive believers away.

115.t: I am here only to give people a clear warning.’

116.t: So they said, ‘Noah, if you do not stop this, you will be stoned.’

117.t: He said, ‘My Lord, my people have rejected me,

118.t: so make a firm judgement between me and them, and save me and my believing followers.’

119.t: So We saved him and his followers in the fully laden ship,

121.t: There truly is a sign in this, though most of them do not believe:

122.t: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.

123.t: The people of Ad, too, called the messengers liars.

124.t: Their brother Hud said to them, ‘Will you not be mindful of God?

125.t: I am a faithful messenger sent to you:

126.t: be mindful of God and obey me.

127.t: I ask no reward of you, for my only reward is with the Lord of the Worlds.

128.t: How can you be so vain that you set up monuments on every high place?

129.t: Do you build fortresses because you hope to be immortal?

130.t: Why do you act like tyrants whenever you attack someone?

131.t: Be mindful of God and obey me;

132.t: be mindful of Him who has provided you with everything you know-

133.t: He has given you livestock, sons,

135.t: for I truly fear that the torment of a grievous day will overtake you.’

136.t: They replied, ‘It makes no difference to us whether you warn us or not,

137.t: for we only do what our forefathers used to do:

139.t: They denounced him as a liar, and so We destroyed them. There truly is a sign in this, though most of them do not believe:

140.t: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.

141.t: The people of Thamud, too, called the messengers liars.

142.t: Their brother Salih said to them, ‘Will you not be mindful of God?

143.t: I am a faithful messenger to you:

144.t: be mindful of God and obey me.

145.t: I ask no reward from you, for my only reward is with the Lord of the Worlds.

146.t: [Do you think] you will be left secure for ever in what you have here-

148.t: fields, palm trees laden with fruit-

149.t: carving your fine houses from the mountains?

150.t: Be mindful of God and obey me:

151.t: do not obey those who are given to excess

152.t: and who spread corruption in the land instead of doing what is right.’

154.t: You are nothing but a man like us. Show us a sign, if you are telling the truth.’

155.t: He said, ‘Here is a camel. She should have her turn to drink and so should you, each on a specified day,

156.t: so do not harm her, or the punishment of a terrible day will befall you.’

157.t: But they hamstrung her. In the morning they had cause to regret it:

158.t: the punishment fell upon them. There truly is a sign in this, though most of them will not believe:

159.t: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.

160.t: The people of Lot, too, called the messengers liars.

161.t: Their brother Lot said to them, ‘Will you not be mindful of God?

162.t: I am a faithful messenger to you:

163.t: be mindful of God and obey me.

164.t: I ask no reward from you, for my only reward is with the Lord of the Worlds.

165.t: Must you, unlike [other] people, lust after males

166.t: and abandon the wives that God has created for you? You are exceeding all bounds,’

167.t: but they replied, ‘Lot! If you do not stop this, you will be driven away.’

168.t: So he said, ‘I loathe what you do:

169.t: Lord, save me and my family from what they are doing.’

170.t: We saved him and all his family,

171.t: except for an old woman who stayed behind,

173.t: and poured a rain of destruction down upon them. How dreadful that rain was for those who had been forewarned!

174.t: There truly is a sign in this, though most of them will not believe:

175.t: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.

176.t: The forest-dwellers, too, called the messengers liars.

177.t: Shuayb said to them, ‘Will you not be mindful of God?

178.t: I am a faithful messenger to you:

179.t: be mindful of God and obey me.

180.t: I ask no reward of you, for my only reward is with the Lord of the Worlds.

181.t: Give full measure: do not sell others short.

183.t: do not deprive people of what is theirs. Do not spread corruption on earth.

184.t: Be mindful of God who created you and former generations,’

186.t: You are nothing but a man like us. In fact we think you are a liar.

187.t: Make bits of the heavens fall down on us, if you are telling the truth.’

188.t: He said, ‘My Lord knows best what you do.’

189.t: They called him a liar, and so the torment of the Day of Shadow came upon them- it was the torment of a terrible day.

190.t: There truly is a sign in this, though most of them will not believe:

191.t: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.

192.t: Truly, this Quran has been sent down by the Lord of the Worlds:

193.t: the Trustworthy Spirit brought it down

194.t: to your heart [Prophet], so that you could bring warning

196.t: This was foretold in the scriptures of earlier religions.

197.t: Is it not proof enough for them that the learned men of the Children of Israel have recognized it?

198.t: If We had sent it down to someone who was not an Arab,

199.t: and he had recited it to them, they still would not have believed in it.

200.t: So We make it pass straight through the hearts of the guilty:

201.t: they will not believe in it until they see the grievous torment,

202.t: which will suddenly hit them when they are not expecting it,

203.t: and then they will say, ‘Can we have more time?’

204.t: How can they ask that Our punishment be brought to them sooner?

205.t: Think, if we let them enjoy this life for some years

206.t: and then the promised torment came upon them,

207.t: what good would their past enjoyment be to them?

208.t: Never have We destroyed a town without sending down messengers to warn it,

209.t: as a reminder from Us: We are never unjust.

210.t: It was not the jinn who brought down this Quran:

211.t: it is neither in their interests nor in their power,

212.t: indeed they are prevented from overhearing it.

213.t: So [Prophet] do not invoke any gods beside God, or you will incur punishment.

215.t: and lower your wing tenderly over the believers who follow you.

216.t: If they disobey you, say, ‘I bear no responsibility for your actions.’

217.t: Put your trust in the Almighty, the Merciful,

218.t: who sees you when you stand up [for prayer]

219.t: and sees your movements among the worshippers:

220.t: He is the All Hearing, the All Knowing.

221.t: Shall I tell you who the jinn come down to?

222.t: They come down to every lying sinner

223.t: who readily lends an ear to them, and most of them are liars:

224.t: only those who are lost in error follow the poets.

225.t: Do you not see how they rove aimlessly in every valley;

226.t: how they say what they do not do?

227.t: Not so those [poets] who believe, do good deeds, remember God often, and defend themselves after they have been wronged. The evildoers will find out what they will return to.
